provenance.instrument: Maidencreek Township Zoning Ordinance of 2017 (Chapter 220 Zoning, Ord. No. 243 of 3-27-2017, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 MA2839, Township of Maidencreek, Berks County (220-11 'Board of Supervisors'). District use lists and lot, yard and height figures are text in Articles IV to XV. The Table of Uses is a PDF attachment that 'shall not change, supersede or modify in any way the actual text' (220-125), so it was not opened. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 117. New Laws: Ord. No. 262 (Environmental Advisory Council), not on zoning
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 04-10-2025.' New Laws: one, Ord. No. 262 of 2026-04-09 (Environmental Advisory Council)
checks: 'In law quarters, an accessory apartment for relatives, shall be permitted as a conditional use subject to Board of Supervisors approval' in the AP, R-1 and R-2 districts 'for single-family detached dwellings' (220-83). The Board of Supervisors decides after a hearing and a Planning Commission review, and the application needs a plan with the preliminary plan information of Chapter 190 (220-111A, C, D)

Only relatives of the occupants may live there, at most two people, and the quarters may have at most 1,000 sq ft of living space (220-83B, C, E). 'The in-law quarters can not be permitted a detached structure to the principal residence (guest house) or constructed above an existing or proposed detached garage' (220-83D)

The quarters must connect to the house's sewage disposal and water supply. The owner must show public water and sewer, or that the existing on-lot sewage system and well can serve the house and the quarters (220-83F)

One added off-street space beyond the house's two (220-83G, 220-61E(4)(a)). The zoning permit is reviewed every two years. When relatives no longer live there the space must become part of the house again and may not be rented as an apartment (220-83H, I)

The quarters are 'an accessory living component or living area of a permitted single-family detached dwelling on an approved lot, which complies with the minimum and maximum dimensional requirements' of the district (220-83A). In AP a residential lot may not be larger than 1.5 acres unless the extra area is needed for on-site water and sewage (220-17B)

R-2a, R-3, R-4 and CR permit single-family dwellings but do not list in-law quarters. C-1, C-2, I and SIA permit no single-family dwelling. In I, accessory uses include 'an accessory dwelling unit for a caretaker or night watchman' (220-48A(16))

Two-family dwellings are permitted by right in R-2, R-2a, R-3, R-4 and CR. 'A single-family detached dwelling containing an accessory apartment shall not be deemed a two-family dwelling' (220-11 'Dwelling'). A 'two-family conversion' of an existing single-family house is defined, but no district lists it (220-11)

'More than one principal structure may be placed on a single lot', if each could be split onto its own lot that meets the district minimums and yards (220-55C). The district sections also allow additional dwellings on a lot when each meets the figures per unit of use (220-23A(1), 220-26A(1), 220-29A(1), 220-32A(2), 220-35A(2))

In AP the number of dwellings on a tract follows a sliding scale that counts existing dwellings: two under 20 acres, three to 50 acres, four to 100 acres (220-17A). Whether in-law quarters count as a dwelling unit there is not settled

Accessory buildings: not in a required front yard, at least 5 ft from the house, at most 25 ft tall and lower than their distance to the nearest lot line (220-58A). Most district tables cap an accessory structure at 10% of the lot

Floodplain (Chapter 117): within any identified floodplain area no new construction or development within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of a watercourse unless DEP's regional office issues a permit (117-17H, 117-21D). New residential construction and substantial improvements need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (117-22A). The Board of Supervisors hears floodplain variances (117-31)
Steep slopes: no residential building on slopes of 25% or more, and no more than half of the minimum lot may be steep slope land (220-60C, D)

Nonconforming lot of record: a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings may be built though the lot is short of area or width, if the yards are met (220-104A). A nonconforming building may grow by up to 25% of its floor area (220-106A)
No use variance bar was found. The Zoning Hearing Board decides variances on the hardship findings of 220-119F
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Maidencreek Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Articles IV to XV (C-1 area figures, C-2 design standards and I and SIA area figures skimmed), 220-55 to 220-61, 220-83, 220-84, Articles XVII, XIX and XX, 220-111, 220-11 from 'Access drive' to 'Impervious surface coverage' and the definitions of in-law quarters and two-family conversions, Chapter 117 to 117-34 'Flood', the New Laws and Notes pages and code searches. Not read: 220-62 to 220-82, 220-85 to 220-102 (220-71 planned residential developments, 220-87 agricultural use rules), the rest of Article XVIII, the rest of 220-11, Chapter 190 and the Table of Uses (PDF).

status.note: A conditional use for relatives of the occupants of the house

status_outside.note: R-2a, R-3, R-4 and CR permit single-family dwellings but do not list in-law quarters

status_by_form.note: 'The in-law quarters can not be permitted a detached structure to the principal residence (guest house) or constructed above an existing or proposed detached garage.' A unit in a detached garage is in a detached structure

path.note: Board of Supervisors after a public hearing, with Planning Commission review (220-111C, D)

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2, R-2a, R-3, R-4, CR)
value.conditions: A freestanding building with two dwelling units, side by side or one over the other (220-11 'Dwelling' B). The district lot figures apply, many of them per unit of use: with public water and sewer 10,000 sq ft in R-2, R-3, R-4 and CR, 8,750 sq ft per unit (5,000 for a semidetached unit) in R-2a. With an on-site system 1.5 acres. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit
value.note: A two-unit building, not a unit added to a house. A 'two-family conversion' of an existing house is defined but not listed, and a house with an accessory apartment is not a two-family dwelling. Whether the lot area counts once or once for each unit is for the zoning officer

value.name: Another principal dwelling on the lot (R-1)
value.conditions: More than one principal structure may stand on a lot if each could be split onto its own lot meeting the district minimum lot and yards (220-55C), on a public or approved private street (220-55D). In R-1 that is 2 acres and 175 ft of width for each dwelling, so 4 acres for two
value.note: A second house on the lot. Whether a land development plan under Chapter 190 is also needed is not settled

value.name: Another principal dwelling on the lot (R-2, R-2a, R-3, R-4, CR)
value.conditions: More than one principal structure may stand on a lot if each could be split onto its own lot meeting the district minimum lot and yards (220-55C), on a public or approved private street (220-55D). That is 1.5 acres for each dwelling with an on-site system. With public water and sewer it is 10,000 sq ft for each (8,750 in R-2a)
value.note: A second house on the lot. The lot must hold the district figures twice over. Whether a land development plan under Chapter 190 is also needed is not settled

requires_conforming_lot.note: 'on an approved lot, which complies with the minimum and maximum dimensional requirements as well as the utility provisions' of the district. Whether 'which complies' describes the lot or the quarters is a reading, so it is a condition, not a bar

historic_bypass.note: No historic district or historic path was found

districts_read_no_listing.note: R-2a, R-3, R-4 and CR permit single-family dwellings without in-law quarters. C-1, C-2, I and SIA permit no single-family dwelling

value.condition: Sewage disposal and water supply for the quarters must be physically connected to the systems serving the house. The owner must show public water and sewer, or that the existing on-lot sewage system and well can serve the house and the quarters. The Sewage Enforcement Officer may review the connections.

The district tables give lot area 'per unit of use' and allow additional dwellings on a lot only when each meets the figures, and in AP a sliding scale counts the dwelling units on a tract. In-law quarters are defined as an accessory dwelling unit but treated as part of the house (220-83A). Whether they need their own lot area is not settled.

Cluster development (conditional use in R-1 and R-2, at least four acres with public sewer and water): lots of 8,000 sq ft and 70 ft wide, building setback 40 ft, rear yard 30 ft, side yards 20 ft together and 10 ft on one side, lot coverage 25%, 35 ft.

Within any identified floodplain area 'no new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse' unless DEP's regional office issues a permit.

In a floodway no encroachment, new construction or substantial improvement unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction without a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway the rise may be at most one foot. New construction and substantial improvement need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation.

On slopes of 25% or more 'no residential, commercial or industrial buildings shall be permitted to be located'. Earthmoving on such slopes needs a plan approved by the County Conservation Service and the Board of Supervisors.

types_allowed.note: 'an accessory living component or living area of a permitted single-family detached dwelling'. Not a detached structure and not above a detached garage

max_sqft.note: 'may not have a gross floor area in excess of 1,000 square feet of living space, which may include a living room, kitchen, bedroom and bathroom'

family_only.note: 'An in-law quarter shall only be utilized by relatives of the occupants of the residence.'

occupancy.value: Relatives of the occupants of the house, at most two people. It may not be rented out as an apartment when relatives no longer live there

owner_occupancy.note: The rule ties the occupants to the household, not to an owner

spaces_required.note: 'a minimum of one additional off-street parking space shall be required for the in-law quarters'

total_on_site.note: Two spaces for the house and one for the quarters

fraction_rounding.note: A fraction is rounded to the nearest whole number, and 'fractional values of exactly 0.5 shall be rounded up'

min_lot_sqft.note: Residential use, single-family home: 1.5 acres, 150 ft wide. 1.5 acres is also the maximum lot area, unless a larger lot is needed for on-site water and sewage (220-17B(1)). Dwellings on a tract follow the sliding scale of 220-17A

'Minimum lot area per unit of use 2 acres', 175 ft wide. The table's only column is headed 'All uses where water supply and/or sewage disposal is on site'. It gives no other figures for a lot with public water and sewer
